title: The force for a wider circle
hook: Change turn radius and predict centripetal force.
misconception: centripetal force doubles when turn radius doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply F_c = mv²/r to compare centripetal force when turn radius changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With uniform circular motion with fixed mass and speed, F_c = mv²/r. When turn radius doubles, centripetal force becomes ½ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model F_c = mv²/r; scaling exponent -1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider uniform circular motion with fixed mass and speed, with a nonzero initial result. If turn radius triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on centripetal force?
recall.why: Apply F_c = mv²/r under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/3.
